cards.power: MCA Stroke — Target's contralateral face and arm are paralyzed.
cards.lore: The leg representation descends into the interhemispheric fissure. Bilateral ACA territory ischemia mimics spinal cord disease.
cards.gradeReason: Gorilla-brain homunculus instantly embodied; contralateral paralysis is a crisp performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anatomical illustration. Subject: giant gorilla straddling a brain cortex, face and arm zones glowing. Mood: authoritative.

cards.power: Conduction Aphasia — Target speaks fluently but cannot repeat a single word. Broca builds speech (expressive). Wernicke understands it (receptive).
cards.lore: The arcuate fasciculus connects both speech hubs. Damage between them causes Conduction Aphasia — fluent speech, intact comprehension, broken repetition.
cards.gradeReason: Two-in-one card; fluent-but-can't-repeat is vivid but splitting two characters dilutes instant embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon duo. Subject: parrot and megaphone duo connected by a fraying arcuate wire, sound waves collapsing. Mood: chaotic verbose.

cards.power: Frontal Release — Re-equips primitive grasp and rooting reflexes.
cards.lore: Irritative lesion (seizures) makes eyes look AWAY. Destructive lesion (stroke) makes eyes look TOWARD the lesion.
cards.gradeReason: Eye gaze rule is clinically crisp; primitive reflex release is fun but needs framing to perform at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nautical illustration. Subject: octopus in captain's hat triggering a grasping reflex in a confused opponent. Mood: commanding executive.

cards.power: Hemispatial Neglect — The left half of the opponent's world ceases to exist.
cards.lore: Dominant side handles math and fingers (Gerstmann). Non-dominant side integrates the spatial map.
cards.gradeReason: Half the world ceasing to exist is immediate, performable, and unforgettable. G1 knockout.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surrealist illustration. Subject: owl in VR goggles with left half of visual field erased to white. Mood: eerie absent.

cards.power: Uncal Herniation — Crush CN III to dilate the pupil, then cause false-localizing hemiplegia.
cards.lore: Hippocampus encodes memory. The Uncus herniates through the tentorium to cause the blown pupil.
cards.gradeReason: Blown pupil as a power move is instantly dramatic and clinically testable — pure G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: retro horror. Subject: elephant reading a book, one eye exploding wide, brain slipping downward through tentorial notch. Mood: ominous urgent.

cards.power: Macular Sparing — MCA/PCA dual blood supply protects central vision during PCA stroke.
cards.lore: Meyer's loop damage is pie in the sky (superior defect). Parietal optic radiation damage is pie on the floor (inferior).
cards.gradeReason: Pie in the sky / pie on the floor is brilliant but requires visual field anatomy context to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: color-wheel illustration. Subject: chameleon with half-erased visual field and pie-chart eyes. Mood: kaleidoscopic precise.

cards.power: Autonomic Arrhythmia — Manipulate internal body state and cardiac rhythm.
cards.lore: Buried deep in the Sylvian fissure. Right insular stroke triggers sympathetic storms and arrhythmias.
cards.gradeReason: Hidden lobe identity is atmospheric; cardiac rhythm manipulation needs contextual framing at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hidden chamber. Subject: stopwatch-wielding turtle buried inside folded brain rock, lightning bolts radiating. Mood: secretive electric.

cards.power: Anterograde Amnesia — Opponent cannot form new declarative memories.
cards.lore: Mammillary body atrophy (Wernicke-Korsakoff) permanently breaks the Papez episodic memory circuit.
cards.gradeReason: Can't form new memories — one of the most viscerally performable cards in medical education.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink and wash. Subject: ferret clutching a broken clock, surrounded by fading footprints and blank notepads. Mood: ethereal haunted.

cards.power: Direct vs Indirect — Dopamine strengthens the direct (go) and weakens the indirect (stop).
cards.lore: Parkinson's loses dopamine (stuck in stop). Huntington's loses the indirect pathway early (stuck in go).
cards.gradeReason: Go/stop logic is elegant but the D1/D2 mechanism is mechanical; needs player familiarity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: steampunk engineering. Subject: praying mantis at a dopamine throttle, two pathway dials labeled GO and STOP. Mood: calibrated mechanical.

cards.power: Dejerine-Roussy — Inflict burning, dysaesthetic pain weeks after a VPL infarct.
cards.lore: Every sensory modality except smell must synapse here before reaching the cortex.
cards.gradeReason: Burning pain weeks later is vivid but Dejerine-Roussy requires named syndrome recognition.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tollbooth illustration. Subject: bulldog guard in STOP vest at a sensory relay station, sparking signal lines around him. Mood: bureaucratic painful.

cards.power: Romberg Fall — Opponent falls over the moment they close their eyes.
cards.lore: Fine touch and proprioception ascend ipsilaterally and do not cross until the medial lemniscus in the medulla.
cards.gradeReason: Close your eyes, fall over — clinically immediate, perfectly performable, no explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: balancing act illustration. Subject: cat poised on a spine column, eyes shut, tipping sideways. Mood: precarious falling.

cards.power: Cape Distribution — Syringomyelia expands the central canal, cutting the crossing fibers.
cards.lore: Pain and temperature cross the midline almost immediately in the anterior commissure of the spinal cord.
cards.gradeReason: Cape distribution is spatially vivid; syrinx mechanism needs explanation for non-med players.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: adventure map. Subject: porcupine in a burning cape crossing midline on a spinal cord cross-section map. Mood: scorched dramatic.

cards.power: UMN Spasticity — Inflict hyperreflexia, spasticity, and a positive Babinski sign. No wasting.
cards.lore: The internal capsule is the bottleneck. A tiny lacunar infarct here causes massive, dense contralateral hemiplegia.
cards.gradeReason: UMN vs LMN is the essential clinical distinction; hyperreflexia + Babinski is instantly testable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: power-lifter illustration. Subject: gorilla flexing through a narrow internal capsule bottleneck, foot extended upward. Mood: dense overwhelming.

cards.power: Intention Tremor — Opponent's movements worsen as they approach the target.
cards.lore: Output crosses to the contralateral thalamus, then the corticospinal tract crosses back. Net result: ipsilateral control.
cards.gradeReason: Movements worsening as you approach the target — perfect game mechanic and immediately embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: confused spider chart. Subject: spider reaching for a fly, limbs shaking violently at the last inch. Mood: twitchy frustrated.

cards.power: Decerebrate vs Decorticate — Dictate the opponent's coma posture based on lesion height.
cards.lore: Cortical loss = decorticate (arms flexed). Lesion below red nucleus = decerebrate (all limbs extended).
cards.gradeReason: Posturing as a power concept is vivid; cortex vs red nucleus distinction needs explaining.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: boxing ring. Subject: kangaroo with a red nucleus glowing in chest, opponent rigid below in decerebrate extension. Mood: knockout hierarchical.

cards.power: ASA Syndrome — Paraplegia and pain loss below lesion, but proprioception survives.
cards.lore: The anterior spinal artery feeds motor and pain tracts. The posterior spinal arteries feed the dorsal columns.
cards.gradeReason: Proprioception-spared paraplegia is clinically crisp; ASA vascular anatomy needs context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cross-section diagram. Subject: angry faces inside spinal cord slice, anterior half scorched and posterior half pristine. Mood: dissociated.

cards.power: The Cleanest Cut — Ipsilateral motor/proprioception loss, contralateral pain loss.
cards.lore: The ultimate test of crossing rules. Pain crosses early, motor and touch cross late.
cards.gradeReason: Split hemisection deficits are the testable classic — players immediately know what to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: butcher diagram. Subject: sheep sliced cleanly in half, left side motor-dead, right side flame-insensate. Mood: precise anatomical.

cards.power: Sphincter Sabotage — Saddle anesthesia and loss of anal tone demands urgent surgery.
cards.lore: Conus = UMN signs mixed with LMN bladder. Cauda Equina = Pure LMN flaccid weakness and areflexia.
cards.gradeReason: Sphincter Sabotage + saddle anesthesia = unforgettable emergency. Instant G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: emergency alert. Subject: aggressive badger in surgical scrubs with a saddle-shaped numb zone glowing red. Mood: urgent alarming.

cards.power: Weber's Strike — Ipsilateral CN III palsy + contralateral hemiplegia.
cards.lore: Houses the cerebral peduncles and oculomotor nerves. Parinaud's syndrome (pineal tumor) blocks upgaze.
cards.gradeReason: Weber's syndrome is named and learnable; CN III + hemiplegia combo needs clinical context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: primate anatomy. Subject: lemur dangling with one eye blown wide and contralateral arm paralyzed. Mood: crossed paradoxical.

cards.power: Locked-In Syndrome — Bilateral ventral destruction leaves only vertical gaze and blinking.
cards.lore: The center for horizontal gaze. An MLF lesion causes Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia (INO).
cards.gradeReason: Locked-In is viscerally dramatic — only blink and look up. Instant table performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cage illustration. Subject: beaver trapped in glass box, eyes darting upward only, body completely motionless. Mood: terrifying trapped.

cards.power: Wallenberg's Curse (Lateral Medulla) — Ipsilateral face pain, Horner's, hoarseness, and ataxia.
cards.lore: Controls breathing (pre-Bötzinger). Lesions here are life-threatening.
cards.gradeReason: Wallenberg's is the classic multi-symptom syndrome — each deficit traceable, immediately performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nautical map. Subject: pelican with droopy eye, ataxic posture, holding a fish that has crossed sides. Mood: doomed elegant.

cards.power: Pupillary Light Reflex — CN II senses the light, bilateral Edinger-Westphal nuclei send CN III to constrict.
cards.lore: A painful third nerve palsy with a blown pupil is a posterior communicating artery aneurysm emergency.
cards.gradeReason: Bilateral EW nuclei mechanism is explanatory, not performative; four cranial nerves in one card is dense.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: binocular illustration. Subject: monkey inspecting a blown pupil through a naval telescope in emergency light. Mood: diagnostic urgent.

cards.power: Bell's vs Stroke — LMN VII palsy drops the whole face. UMN spares the forehead.
cards.lore: CN VII has the longest intracranial course. An isolated CN VI palsy is a false localizing sign for raised ICP.
cards.gradeReason: Forehead-sparing vs full drop is instantly testable and performable — perfect bedside rule.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dog portrait. Subject: bloodhound with full left face drooping, forehead intact on right, wearing a stethoscope. Mood: diagnostic comparative.

cards.power: Jugular Foramen Mass — Compress IX, X, and XI to destroy swallowing and shoulder shrug.
cards.lore: Uvula deviates AWAY from a CN X lesion. Tongue deviates TOWARD a CN XII LMN lesion.
cards.gradeReason: Away/toward deviation rule is a great mnemonic; jugular foramen grouping needs anatomical context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: swamp illustration. Subject: frog choking at a compressed jugular foramen, tongue veering sideways, uvula fleeing. Mood: dysfunctional absurd.

cards.power: Archicerebellum Spin — Flocculonodular lobe lesions destroy balance and trigger nystagmus.
cards.lore: Vermis controls the trunk (paleocerebellum). Lateral hemispheres control distal limbs (neocerebellum).
cards.gradeReason: Archicerebellum Spin is evocative; FDGE deep nuclei stat needs table context to perform fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: steampunk hummingbird. Subject: mechanical hummingbird navigating a cerebellar folia maze, eyes spinning with nystagmus. Mood: precise whirring.

cards.power: Test of Skew — Differentiate a benign inner ear from a posterior circulation stroke.
cards.lore: Pure vertical nystagmus is ALWAYS central. Direction-changing horizontal nystagmus is central.
cards.gradeReason: Test of Skew is an immediately performable clinical act — look for the difference, report it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon cat in a fez. Subject: dizzy cat spinning in water rings, one eye higher than the other. Mood: swirling differentiated.

cards.power: Waiter's Tip (Erb's Palsy) — C5/C6 upper trunk avulsion during shoulder dystocia.
cards.lore: Lower trunk (C8/T1) injury causes Klumpke's claw hand PLUS Horner syndrome from T1 sympathetic drag.
cards.gradeReason: Waiter's Tip is instantly embodyable — arm hangs, hand pronated, you know exactly what to mime.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: art nouveau. Subject: squid with upper tentacles fused in waiter's-tip posture, lower tentacles clawing. Mood: awkward subservient.

cards.power: Spiral Groove Crush — Target loses wrist and finger extension, but preserves elbow extension.
cards.lore: The triceps motor branch is given off BEFORE the nerve wraps around the humeral shaft.
cards.gradeReason: Wrist drop is vivid; preserved elbow extension distinction requires anatomical knowledge.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wildlife illustration. Subject: vulture slumped on a park bench, wrist dropped, elbow still extended. Mood: hungover precise.

cards.power: Ulnar Paradox — A wrist lesion creates a WORSE claw than an elbow lesion.
cards.lore: A high lesion paralyzes FDP, meaning the fingers can't flex to form the full claw.
cards.gradeReason: The paradox is immediately counterintuitive and testable — players will argue about it, which is the point.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: comic sloth. Subject: sloth holding a newspaper, wrist bent in paradoxical worse claw than elbow position. Mood: paradoxically worse.

cards.power: Carpal Tunnel Crush — Nocturnal paraesthesia in the lateral 3.5 digits.
cards.lore: Thenar wasting means the nerve is dying. Benediction hand only happens with a high (elbow) lesion.
cards.gradeReason: Waking up with numb fingers is universal; lateral 3.5 digit precision and LOAF muscles need context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: precision illustration. Subject: chimp with the OK sign and thenar eminence fading, moonlit background. Mood: nocturnal precise.

cards.power: Psoas Hematoma — Compress the nerve within the psoas to kill hip flexion and knee extension.
cards.lore: Absent knee jerk + positive femoral stretch test + anterior thigh numbness.
cards.gradeReason: Psoas hematoma mechanism is vivid; L2-L4 myotome pattern needs clinical familiarity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: flamingo anatomy. Subject: flamingo with one leg collapsed, chair tipped, knee jerk hammer flying away. Mood: buckled elegant.

cards.power: Foot Drop — Common peroneal palsy loses dorsiflexion and eversion.
cards.lore: How to tell peroneal palsy from L5 root lesion? L5 also loses inversion (tibialis posterior).
cards.gradeReason: Foot drop is universally recognized and immediately performable — steppage gait needs no explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: equine anatomy. Subject: horse with bandaged fibular neck, hoof dragging on scorched earth. Mood: hobbled determined.

cards.power: Sensory Level — Pinpoint the exact spinal segment of a cord transection.
cards.lore: The thumb is C6. The middle finger is C7. The pinky is C8. Always.
cards.gradeReason: C6/C7/C8 finger mnemonic is excellent; sensory level clinical test needs patient framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: postal map. Subject: zebra with dermatome stripes labelled like postal codes, thumb glowing C6. Mood: indexed precise.

cards.power: Jendrassik Manoeuvre — Pull clasped hands apart to amplify gamma motor neuron activity.
cards.lore: Hyperreflexia + Clonus + Babinski = UMN lesion. Areflexia + Wasting = LMN lesion.
cards.gradeReason: Pull your hands apart — the Jendrassik is physically performable at the table right now.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: action sports. Subject: kangaroo yanking clasped hands apart, reflex hammer orbiting like a satellite. Mood: kinetic amplified.

cards.power: Adrenal Bypass — The adrenal medulla acts as a modified sympathetic ganglion, releasing directly to blood.
cards.lore: Sympathetic preganglionics are short. Parasympathetic preganglionics are long.
cards.gradeReason: Adrenal medulla as bypassed ganglion is mechanistic physiology — explains rather than invites performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fire-and-water duality. Subject: two llamas, one breathing fire asleep, one chewing grass awake, adrenal gland between them. Mood: balanced physiologic.

cards.power: Hydroxyamphetamine Test — Dilates central and preganglionic lesions, fails in postganglionic.
cards.lore: Ptosis, Miosis, Anhidrosis. An acute Horner with neck pain is a carotid dissection until proven otherwise.
cards.gradeReason: Ptosis/Miosis/Anhidrosis triad is clinical gold; hydroxyamphetamine test mechanics need pharmacology context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ophidian portrait. Subject: cobra with droopy eye, constricted pupil, and a dry face, three neurons visible in chain. Mood: quiet ominous.

cards.power: Spurling's Shock — Axial compression of rotated neck reproduces cervical radicular pain.
cards.lore: Posterolateral disc herniations in the lumbar spine compress the exiting nerve root ONE LEVEL BELOW the disc.
cards.gradeReason: Spurling's sign is a physical manoeuvre you can perform on another player — pure G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: forensic anatomy. Subject: fox grabbing its own neck and pressing down, lightning bolts shooting down one arm. Mood: electric diagnostic.

cards.power: Dying Back (Length-Dependent) — The longest axons fail first, causing stocking-glove sensory loss.
cards.lore: Guillain-Barré Syndrome shows high CSF protein with normal cell counts (dissociation) and absent reflexes.
cards.gradeReason: Stocking-glove numbness working its way up is spatially immediate and viscerally imaginable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: textile illustration. Subject: cat pulling on a dissolving stocking from toe upward, reflexes vanishing behind it. Mood: retreating numb.

cards.power: Hakim's Triad — Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus causes wobbly, wacky, and wet (gait, dementia, incontinence).
cards.lore: Aqueductal stenosis is obstructive. Post SAH failure of arachnoid granulations is communicating.
cards.gradeReason: Wobbly, wacky, and wet is the best mnemonic in the deck — immediately performable and unforgettable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: deep sea diving. Subject: bloated deep-sea fish in diver helmet waddling and leaking, brain chambers illuminated inside. Mood: pressurized confused.

cards.power: Lucid Interval — Epidural hematoma patients wake up, talk, and then suddenly herniate.
cards.lore: Epidural = Arterial (Middle Meningeal), Biconvex. Subdural = Venous (Bridging Veins), Crescent.
cards.gradeReason: Lucid interval is a narrative arc — wake up, chat, herniate. Dramatically performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: three-layer cross-section. Subject: armadillo in layered armor with biconvex and crescent bleeds glowing on either side. Mood: protective catastrophic.

cards.power: False Localization — Contralateral peduncle pushed against tentorial notch causes IPSILATERAL hemiplegia.
cards.lore: A fixed dilated pupil is the earliest reliable clinical sign of uncal herniation (parasympathetic fibers on outside of CN III).
cards.gradeReason: Kernohan's notch producing ipsilateral signs is a great paradox but needs syndrome name context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial press. Subject: pig brain being squeezed through a tentorial notch, ipsilateral leg kicking the wrong way. Mood: pressure paradox.

cards.power: Vasogenic Edema — Bacterial meningitis breaks the tight junctions; water pours in.
cards.lore: Tumor vasculature lacks a blood-brain barrier, which is why gadolinium contrast lights up tumors on MRI.
cards.gradeReason: REJECTED bouncer visual is strong; tight junction mechanism is educational rather than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nightclub bouncer. Subject: bulldog in tuxedo at a REJECTED sign, bacteria forcing the door, gadolinium slipping through tumor side. Mood: selective enforcement.

cards.power: Subclavian Steal — Arm exercise reverses vertebral artery flow, causing posterior circulation ischemia.
cards.lore: Sudden unilateral deafness + facial numbness + contralateral body numbness = AICA stroke.
cards.gradeReason: Subclavian Steal is immediately performable — wave your arm and steal your brain's blood supply.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: plumbing diagram. Subject: octopus reversing a vertebral artery pipe while exercising, posterior brain going dark. Mood: siphoning ischemic.

cards.power: Thunderclap Headache — Saccular aneurysm rupture into subarachnoid space.
cards.lore: A painful CN III palsy is a Posterior Communicating Artery (PCoA) aneurysm until proven otherwise.
cards.gradeReason: Thunderclap headache — worst headache of your life — is instantly performable and dramatically compelling.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: horror comic. Subject: bat on a branch holding a ticking bomb, one eye blown wide, thunderclap explosion above. Mood: catastrophic inevitable.

cards.power: The Great Mimic — Cerebral Venous Thrombosis causes raised ICP, seizures, and focal deficits.
cards.lore: Treat with anticoagulation (LMWH) even if the venous infarct has already caused hemorrhagic transformation.
cards.gradeReason: Great Mimic framing is compelling; CVT's anticoagulate-despite-hemorrhage rule needs clinical grounding.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sewer pipe illustration. Subject: walrus plugging a venous drain, brain pressure gauge in red, empty delta sign missing above. Mood: obstructed mimicking.

cards.power: Central Cord Syndrome — Hyperextension in elderly patients destroys the central cervical cord.
cards.lore: Arm motor fibers lie centrally, leg fibers lie peripherally. Therefore, arms are much weaker than legs.
cards.gradeReason: Summary card — describes anatomy and syndrome without inviting embodiment or performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: comparative anatomy. Subject: giraffe with central cord highlighted, arms barely moving while legs stride normally. Mood: differential hierarchical.

cards.power: Neurogenic Claudication — Spinal stenosis causes bilateral leg pain when walking, relieved by bending forward.
cards.lore: In the cervical spine, the root exits ABOVE its numbered vertebra. In the lumbar spine, it exits BELOW.
cards.gradeReason: Bending forward to relieve pain is immediately physically demonstrable and memorable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dachshund anatomy. Subject: long dachshund with compressed spine bending forward into relief, legs cramping behind. Mood: positional relief.

cards.power: REM Intrusion — Loss of orexin drops the patient directly from wakefulness to atonic REM sleep (Cataplexy).
cards.lore: The VLPO and ARAS mutually inhibit each other. Orexin from the lateral hypothalamus stabilizes the awake state.
cards.gradeReason: Collapsing straight into REM is vivid; flip-flop switch mechanism needs neurochemistry context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pajama illustration. Subject: bear mid-conversation collapsing into boneless REM sleep, orexin molecules disappearing overhead. Mood: sudden atonic.

cards.power: Gate Control Theory Activate large A-beta touch fibers to inhibit C fiber pain transmission.
cards.lore: Referred pain happens because visceral and somatic afferents converge on the exact same dorsal horn neurons.
cards.gradeReason: Rub it to feel better is intuitive; gate control mechanism at dorsal horn level is explanatory.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gate mechanism. Subject: raccoon rubbing its wounded paw, a gate slamming shut on incoming pain signals. Mood: modulatory relief.

cards.power: Pie in the Sky — Anterior temporal lobectomy damages Meyer's loop, causing superior quadrantanopia.
cards.lore: The macula occupies 50% of the primary visual cortex, explaining central vision sparing in PCA strokes.
cards.gradeReason: Pie in the sky / pie on the floor is one of the most spatially vivid mnemonics in neuroanatomy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: visual field diagram. Subject: mantis with upper visual field replaced by floating pie slice, lower field intact. Mood: superior absent.

cards.power: One-and-a-Half Syndrome — PPRF + MLF lesion on same side. Only contralateral abduction survives.
cards.lore: MLF lesions cause INO (adduction failure). Bilateral INO in a young patient is Multiple Sclerosis until proven otherwise.
cards.gradeReason: One-and-a-half syndrome is clinically elegant; PPRF + MLF anatomy requires dedicated neurology context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: amphibian portrait. Subject: frog with one eye frozen and one half-drifted, only the abducting eye free. Mood: constrained lateral.

cards.power: Transient Global Amnesia — Sudden anterograde amnesia caused by venous backflow hitting the hippocampus.
cards.lore: Hippocampus is essential for encoding. Remote memories survive hippocampal destruction due to systems consolidation.
cards.gradeReason: TGA is a vivid narrative; venous backflow mechanism and systems consolidation need clinical framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: goldfish memory. Subject: goldfish in detective coat reading the same book over and over, hippocampus sputtering. Mood: looping bewildered.

cards.power: Pan-hypopituitarism — Craniopharyngioma crushes the stalk, destroying endocrine and autonomic control.
cards.lore: Lateral hypothalamus = hunger (orexin). Ventromedial = satiety. Suprachiasmatic = master clock.
cards.gradeReason: Stalk crush mechanism is explanatory anatomy; SLAM DR nuclei stat is opaque without a key.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: homeostasis dashboard. Subject: lizard at a control panel with hunger/satiety/clock dials, stalk being crushed by a tumor shape. Mood: regulatory failing.

cards.power: Apoplexy — Sudden hemorrhage of adenoma causes thunderclap headache and visual loss.
cards.lore: Suprasellar extension hits crossing nasal fibers, causing bitemporal hemianopia (tunnel vision).
cards.gradeReason: Thunderclap + tunnel vision is a crisp two-punch emergency — immediately dramatic and testable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hermit crab portrait. Subject: hermit crab in a sella turcica shell hemorrhaging upward, nasal fibers severed above. Mood: explosive tunnel-visioned.

cards.power: Localize. Name. Explain. — Map the Horner's, the ataxia, and the hoarseness to the exact vessel.
cards.lore: You don't know it until you can trace the wiring backward from the deficit to the lesion without looking it up.
cards.gradeReason: The Attending's power IS the performance of clinical reasoning — localize is an act, not a description.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wise owl professor. Subject: owl in white coat with a brain map, pointing at Wallenberg territory with chalk. Mood: authoritative exacting.

cards.cardName: Uncle FrizzleBob's Rule of the Street
cards.power: Epistemic Sabotage — Destroy the boring format to directly preserve the factual integrity.
cards.lore: You remember stories, not lists, one who knows where a structure lives can predict what happens when it dies.
cards.gradeReason: Meta-card closing the deck is pure FrizzleBob — manifesto as card, instantly embodied as a worldview.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: street art graffiti. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit splashing paint on a boring textbook, kayfabe anatomy glowing beneath. Mood: rebellious revelatory.

verdict: FrizzleBob says: This deck does what most med-ed products are too scared to try — it makes the nervous system into a roster of characters you can fight with. Named syndromes become finishing moves, tracts become combatants, and the Attending closes as a final boss who demands you perform, not recite. Naming is exceptional throughout (Sphincter Sabotage, Wallenberg's Curse, Thunderclap Headache). Weak point: four cards run explanatory rather than performative (Autonomo, Hypothala, Cord Syndromes Summary, Cranio I-IV). Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 56 cards. Every major neuroanatomy structure weaponized. For med students who want to actually remember where things go and what breaks when they die.

notes: 15 pages (1 cover + 14 card pages), 4 cards per page, 56 cards total. Page 2 Broca & Wernicke LORE partially obscured by illustration at extraction resolution — text approximated from context. Three distinct Spino cards: card 12 (Spinothalamic Tract), card 16 (Spinal Cord Cross-Section), card 46 (Spino Cord Syndromes Summary) — all distinct, no duplication. Page backgrounds vary per spread (map/notebook/lab/steampunk) without breaking visual unity. No RAF dice boxes present. ADD in filename likely refers to Additional version suffix.
